_comment: Copy to ~/.claude/crossmodel/crossmodel.config.json to register your own model aliases. IT MUST LIVE IN $HOME: the plugin installs under a versioned path, so a config written into the plugin directory is destroyed by every update and silently reverts you to the built-in aliases. The plugin directory is still searched, as a legacy fallback only. Merged over the built-ins, so reusing a key replaces it. Easiest path: run /crossmodel-setup instead of writing this by hand.

models._comment_models: Aliases are what you type in --model and in routing.json. Keep them short — you will type them constantly.

_comment_providers: Adding a NEW provider needs an args() builder, which JSON cannot express — it belongs in bench/providers.mjs as a pull request. Built in: codex, grok, cursor, opencode, gemini, ollama, claude.
_comment_cursor: Cursor CLI (bin: agent, needs a Cursor subscription; auth with agent login or CURSOR_API_KEY). VERIFIED with a real run on agent 2026.08.11. One alias ships, cgrok -> cursor-grok-4.6-high; agent --list-models is the authority for the rest, and the same subscription carries GPT-5.6 Sol, Claude Opus 5, Kimi K3 and Composer. Reasoning effort is part of the model id (-low/-medium/-high/-xhigh, optional -fast), not a flag, so crossmodel refuses --effort here instead of dropping it. --network is refused too: Cursor sandbox is only enabled|disabled, with no network knob. It writes freely inside --cwd like every provider here — crossmodel passes --force and Cursor's own default sandbox mode. The single rule anywhere is that git history stays the orchestrator's; see lib/permissions.mjs.
_comment_grok: xAI Grok Build (bin: grok, needs SuperGrok or X Premium+). Only the 'grok' alias ships; run 'grok models' to see what your subscription offers and add the rest here. A write run uses its 'workspace' profile — edit in --cwd, read anywhere, run the build. Unlike codex it leaves .git/ writable, so the no-commit rule is a contract rather than a lock: review 'git log' as well as the diff. The argument shape is from the published docs, not from a measured run: verify with 'crossmodel --model grok --cwd /tmp/probe "List the files you can see."' before trusting it.
_comment_opencode: opencode is provider-neutral: it reaches OpenRouter, Ollama, OpenAI, Google and anything OpenAI-compatible through one adapter, so the model string is 'provider/model' as opencode spells it. Run 'opencode models' to see what your install offers. It supports --write under the permission policy in ~/.claude/crossmodel/permissions.json.
